answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with random spot-check audits. Every identity, like a quill signing a ledger, must answer an unpredictable challenge within a short window, proving live control of a unique resource, not a copied credential. The audit is a bridge only a real operator can cross in time: an attacker running a thousand Sybils faces a thousand surprise checks, and each missed one freezes that identity and flags its neighbours. The signal is cheap for one honest agent but ruinous at scale, because audit cost multiplies per identity while honest cost stays flat.
